items.title: Petition demands urgent action as graduate midwives still left without jobs
items.summary: The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) has launched a petition ‘demanding urgent action’ from the Welsh Government as more than 60 midwifery graduates are understood to still be without roles.

items.title: Petition demands action over jobless graduate midwives
items.summary: The Royal College of Midwives has set up a petition calling on the Welsh Government to address shortages of jobs for newly registered midwives.

items.title: Award: BCU-DCO-64076 - REPLACEMENT OF AN AGING NEONATAL INCUBATOR
items.summary: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership-Procurement Services (hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust). Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board have direct awarded a contract for the purchase of a Neonatal Incubator.

items.title: Essex midwives get landmark payout after ‘dangerous’ gas exposure
items.summary: Midwives and maternity staff who were exposed to dangerous levels of gas for years at work in South Essex have received a “landmark” £750,000 pay-out, a union has announced.

items.title: HPV vaccination before pregnancy linked with reduced preterm birth
items.summary: A study has found benefits of HPV vaccination that extend beyond cancer prevention to reduced risk of adverse outcomes in pregnancy. The Swedish analysis showed having a human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine before pregnancy is associated with a lower risk of major pregnancy complications including preterm birth.

items.title: Blue plaque for female medic who pioneered midwifery training
items.summary: A blue plaque will be unveiled next week in London to commemorate the work of a doctor credited with transforming maternity care and midwifery training.

items.title: Independent review of Scotland’s maternity services begins
items.summary: An independent review of maternity services across Scotland has begun, examining how care can be improved for women, babies and families.

items.title: Pregnancy complications ‘linked’ to later cardiovascular and kidney disease
items.summary: Pregnancy complications including preterm birth and miscarriage may indicate an increased risk of future cardiovascular, metabolic and kidney disorders, according to a new UK study.

items.title: Irish graduate nurses and midwives ‘left in limbo’ over job contracts
items.summary: The latest group of nursing and midwifery graduates in Ireland are being left without guaranteed jobs to go to, in spite of hospital vacancies, union leaders have warned.

items.title: Independent review of Scottish maternity services gets underway
items.summary: A nationwide review of Scotland’s maternity services begins today, with the remit of examining how care can be improved for women, babies and families.

items.title: Maternal resilience in crisis: breastfeeding experiences during COVID-19 in Pakistan
items.summary: Background/Aims Breastfeeding is important for the health of both infants and mothers. The COVID-19 pandemic amplified concerns around sustaining breastfeeding, particularly regarding safety when the mother was infected.

items.title: Attending a community weight management organisation during pregnancy: a service evaluation
items.summary: Background/Aims A nutritious diet, regular physical activity and minimising excess weight gain are key during pregnancy. This service evaluation investigated reasons for accessing weight management support during pregnancy and evaluated changes to diet, physical activity and wellbeing.

items.title: Addressing the risk of disproportionate maternal mortality among black and brown women
items.summary: Black and brown women are three times more likely to die in childbirth or up to 6 weeks postpartum compared to their white counterparts. Several critical factors contribute to this inequality, including racism and a predominantly white population in midwifery and education.

items.title: Exploring student midwives' experiences of reflective practice: a qualitative study
items.summary: Background/Aims Reflective practice is a core skill in midwifery, but there is limited research exploring how student midwives experience the reflective learning process. This study aimed to explore this to enhance reflective education. Methods Focus groups were conducted with 20 undergraduate midwifery students.

items.title: Midwives' evaluations of the labour care guide: a cross-sectional study from Türkiye
items.summary: Background/Aims Research on midwives' perceptions of the World Health Organization's labour care guide remains limited, despite its increasing use in intrapartum care.

items.title: New bereavement leave rights
items.summary: British Journal of Midwifery, Volume 34, Issue 10, Page 537-537, October 2026.

items.title: Evidence is ‘reassuring’ for women who become pregnant while taking GLP-1 drugs
items.summary: Exposure to GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs around conception does not appear to be linked to a detectable increase in adverse outcomes for mothers or babies, a large review of the evidence has concluded.

items.title: Study finds no evidence of harm from GLP-1 exposure during pregnancy
items.summary: Women who accidentally become pregnant while taking a GLP-1 treatment for diabetes or weight loss are not at increased risk of miscarriage or other complications of pregnancy, according to new research.

items.title: NMC four-year midwifery strategy targets racism and safety
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has set out a four-year strategy for midwifery regulation aimed at supporting safer maternity care, with equity and anti-racism among its listed priorities.
